exercise.name: Otis-Up

reference.title: Otis-Up
reference.listing: Page could not be read here (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); the movement is taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.

exercise.mechanics: Compound (trunk flexion with an overhead press)

breathing.pattern: Exhale as you sit up and press; inhale as you lower the weight and roll down.

prescription.tempo: 1.7 s up and press, 0.5 s hold, 2.6 s down

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Hold one dumbbell across your chest, squeezed between the palms.
Curl up and keep sitting up while you press the dumbbell toward the ceiling.
At the top, arms straight overhead, chest tall.
Bring the dumbbell back to the chest as you roll down: low back, shoulder blades, head.
Settle on the mat and go again.

mistakes.mistake: Swinging the arms to throw yourself up
mistakes.fix: Curl first; the press rides along with the rise.
Press the heels down or anchor the feet; use a lighter dumbbell.
Roll down slowly with the weight at the chest.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the weight over the face lying down
mistakes.fix: Keep it at the chest until you have curled up.

kinematics.norm: From lying to about 70-80 degrees from the floor (full sit-up range)
Grows as the pelvis rolls toward the thighs (Andersson 1997)
Dumbbell at the chest lying, overhead at the top (clinical opinion)
Dumbbell squeezed between the palms (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #8755, Otis-Up, video (movement reference; page not readable here)

Axler and McGill 1997, low-back loads over a variety of abdominal exercises: searching for the safest abdominal challenge (Med Sci Sports Exerc 29(6):804-811)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Repeated loaded sit-ups put high compression on the lumbar spine (Axler and McGill 1997); keep the load moderate and stop with back pain.
Keep the dumbbell over the chest or above the head, never over the face when lying.
modify: Lighter dumbbell or a plate held at the chest.
Pregnancy, postpartum or diastasis recti: get cleared first, and avoid long supine work later in pregnancy.
regressions: Sit-up with the weight held at the chest (no press).
Crunch with the arms reaching up.

muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis curls the trunk off the mat and controls the way down; the weight pressed toward the ceiling shifts the load (Escamilla 2006 and Axler and McGill 1997 on sit-up muscle demand).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas finishes the sit-up once the trunk is about 30-45 degrees up (Andersson 1997; Axler and McGill 1997).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas finishes the sit-up once the trunk is about 30-45 degrees up (Andersson 1997; Axler and McGill 1997).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Presses the dumbbell from the chest to overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Presses the dumbbell from the chest to overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbows in the press (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_l: Straightens the elbows in the press (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Help curl the trunk and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Help curl the trunk and keep it square (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Rotates the shoulder blade up as the arms go overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Rotates the shoulder blade up as the arms go overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder blade overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Supports the shoulder blade overhead (clinical opinion).
